content: The Centrosomal protein of 63 kDa (CEP63) is a protein encoded by the CEP63 gene in humans. Multiple alternatively spliced transcript variants of this gene have been identified, but their biological significance remains undetermined. This gene encodes a protein that contains six coiled-coil domains. The protein is localized to the centrosome, which is a non-membranous organelle that serves as the primary microtubule-organizing center in animal cells. Recent computational studies have identified a pathogenic property associated with the L61P point mutation in the CEP63 protein, which disrupts its native structural conformation. CEP63 has been demonstrated to interact with several other proteins, including DISC1 (Disrupted in Schizophrenia 1), CEP152 (Centrosomal protein of 152 kDa), and CDK1 (Cyclin-dependent kinase 1).
